    29_plotnine_ggplot

    datar allows applying plotnine's ggplot into the processing pipeline

    In [1]:
    Copied! 
    import datar.all as dr
from datar import f
import pandas as pd
import plotnine as pln

from pathlib import Path

# Get the path object pointing to the ``notebooks`` directory that contains *.csv files 
data_dir = next(Path("/home").rglob("*/notebooks/*.csv")).parent

    In [5]:
    Copied! 
    ##----------------------------------------------------------------------##
##           Use plotnine to draw scatter plot Height ~ Weight          ##
##----------------------------------------------------------------------##

(
    tb_baseball
    >> pln.ggplot()
    + pln.theme_seaborn()
    + pln.geom_point(pln.aes(x="Weight", y="Height", color="Position"))
    + pln.geom_smooth(pln.aes(x="Weight", y="Height"), method="lm", se=False, color="black")
    + pln.ggtitle("Scatter plot Height ~ Weight colored by Position")
    + pln.theme(figure_size=(10, 6)) # width=10, height=6
).show()
    ##----------------------------------------------------------------------## ## Use plotnine to draw scatter plot Height ~ Weight ## ##----------------------------------------------------------------------## ( tb_baseball >> pln.ggplot() + pln.theme_seaborn() + pln.geom_point(pln.aes(x="Weight", y="Height", color="Position")) + pln.geom_smooth(pln.aes(x="Weight", y="Height"), method="lm", se=False, color="black") + pln.ggtitle("Scatter plot Height ~ Weight colored by Position") + pln.theme(figure_size=(10, 6)) # width=10, height=6 ).show()
    In [6]:
    Copied! 
    ##---------------------------------------------------------------------##
##           Use plotnine to draw boxplot Height ~ Position            ##
##---------------------------------------------------------------------##

(
    tb_baseball
    >> pln.ggplot()
    + pln.theme_seaborn()
    + pln.geom_boxplot(pln.aes(x="Position", y="Height", fill="Position"), notch=True)
    + pln.coord_flip()
    + pln.ggtitle("Boxplot Height ~ Position")
    + pln.theme(figure_size=(10, 6)) # width=10, height=6
).show()
    ##---------------------------------------------------------------------## ## Use plotnine to draw boxplot Height ~ Position ## ##---------------------------------------------------------------------## ( tb_baseball >> pln.ggplot() + pln.theme_seaborn() + pln.geom_boxplot(pln.aes(x="Position", y="Height", fill="Position"), notch=True) + pln.coord_flip() + pln.ggtitle("Boxplot Height ~ Position") + pln.theme(figure_size=(10, 6)) # width=10, height=6 ).show()
